issues.legal_issue: A licensee’s continued occupation of a public building after the licence expires or is terminated constitutes unauthorised occupation for the purpose of statutory eviction proceedings.
material_facts: A public corporation owned the building and had allowed the occupant to use it under a licence.
After the occupant defaulted on licence fees, the licence was terminated, but the occupant remained in the building.
An Estate Officer issued notice and ordered eviction under the public-buildings eviction legislation.
The occupant brought a civil suit seeking to prevent eviction under that order.
issues.conclusion: The continued occupation of a public building by a licensee after the licence expires or is determined is unauthorised occupation under Section 2(f) of the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968. The Estate Officer had jurisdiction to order eviction, and the statutory bar on suits challenging the order applied.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(f) covers both occupation without authority from the outset and continued occupation after authority expires or is determined. Its words “whether by way of lease or any other mode of transfer” include a licence. Reading the provision to exclude licensees would defeat the purpose of the speedy statutory remedy. The Court relied on the distinction between lease and licence under Section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and Section 52 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882, and on Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, B.M. Lall v. M/s. Dunlop Rubber Co. (India) Ltd., Qudrat Ullah v. Municipal Board, Bareilly, Khalil Ahmed Bashir Ahmed v. Tufelhussein Samasbhai Sarangpurwala, Ashoka Marketing Ltd. v. Punjab National Bank, M/s. Jain Ink Manufacturing Company v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, and Jiwan Dass v. Life Insurance Corporation of India. The Court also noted the materially similar definition in Section 2(g) of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971. Under Sections 3–5 of the Kerala Act, an Estate Officer may conduct eviction proceedings and order eviction; Section 10 provides an appeal, and Section 15 bars a suit challenging the eviction order.

rule.if: public_building_occupation and occupation_under_license and license_authority_ended and statutory_public_building_eviction_proceeding

predicates.public_building_occupation: A person remained in a building that belonged to or was held by a public authority covered by the applicable eviction scheme.
predicates.occupation_under_license: The public authority had permitted the person to occupy the building under a licence.
predicates.license_authority_ended: The licence expired or was terminated while the person remained in the building.
predicates.statutory_public_building_eviction_proce: An eviction officer proceeded under a statutory scheme for eviction from public buildings.

issues.definition: When a person remains in a public building under a licence whose authority has ended, and an eviction officer proceeds under a statutory public-building eviction scheme, the continued occupation is treated as unauthorized.
